newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: S.Korea's July vehicle sales rise at home, abroad.
newsitem.headline: S.Korea's July vehicle sales rise at home, abroad.

text.p: South Korea's domestic vehicle sales rose to 161,634 in July from 133,591 a year earlier, provisional figures from the Korea Automobile Manufacturers' Association showed on Tuesday.
The association said the nation's vehicle exports totalled a provisional 100,300 in July, up 37 percent from 73,220 a year earlier.
Research analyst Song Sang-hoon at the association said car sales by Kia Motors Corp shot up after the financially troubled company offered a sharp discount.

Kia Motor Sales Co, sales affiliate of the Kia Group, South Korea's eighth largest industrial group, began selling passenger and commercial vehicles at a 29.9 percent cash discount on July 20 to raise funds. The package raised an estimated 350 billion won in the first three days.
The association figures showed Kia's domestic sales totalled 45,222 vehicles in July from 38,556 a year earlier. Its exports rose to 31,990 from 22,964 a year earlier.
South Korea's largest carmaker Hyundai Motor sold 59,418 vehicles at home in July, up 3.4 percent from 57,479 a year earlier. It exported 37,523 vehicles, down from 39,118.

Helped by a series of new car models introduced this year, Daewoo Motor's July vehicle sales jumped to 37,253 in the local market from 15,909 in July last year and to 22,881 units abroad against 7,876.
Domestic vehicle sales for the first seven months fell to 886,517 from 950,866. But the seven-month exports rose to 738,908 from 645,290 a year earlier.
Song said the financial problems of Kia Motors would have a limited impact on South Korean vehicle sales at home and abroad.
"Kia's impact will not be as big as many might worry as the company will continue to produce vehicles," he added.
The association lowered its 1997 domestic vehicle sales forecast to 1.6 million from an earlier projection of 1.7 million. The sales totalled 1.64 million last year.
The association raised its exports forecast to 1.38 million vehicles this year against an earlier projection of 1.35 million and 1.21 million exported last year.
Song said the growth in local car sales would be slow in view of the saturated market. Overseas sales are expected to grow at a faster pace because of expanding production bases abroad, he added.
